# III. THE HIVE
[italic]Last pages. The handwriting gets worse from here.[/italic]
## Shift 18. The walls Pump house, sublevel two. The corridors have grown over. Dark resin, ribbed like the inside of a throat and as hard as fibreglass. On the floor a living mat, warm and damp, that gives a little under the boot. A wounded runner lay down on it and its wounds closed in an hour. The floor feeds them. The floor heals them.
## Shift 19. The night crew Found them. In the walls, sealed upright, resin to the chin. Alive. Some of them were awake. Every one had a dead gripper on the floor by their feet. They are not being stored. They are being used.
Kowalski was third from the left. He asked me for something, and I gave it to him.
## Shift 21. They do not need to talk Two of them across the plaza turned their heads at the same instant, toward a door only one of them could see. One worked out the shutter codes at the pump house, and by the next shift they were all coming through shutters. What one of them learns, all of them know.
## Shift 22. Her Grippers do not lay eggs. Something does. Deeper in, past the walls, the resin thickens and the air is hot as a kitchen, and something very large is breathing down there. When they rest, every one of them faces that way.
[bold]It is not a species. It is one animal wearing many bodies, and she is the middle of it.[/bold]
## Shift 23 The liaison wanted all my notes. Asked whether an egg could be moved safely. Not whether it should be. The case was never a rock sample. Somebody should put that on [netlink="wyleaks.deep" link="wyleaks.deep"].
Some colonists have stopped running. They leave the clinic doors open at night. I watched one of them kneel at the resin.
## Shift 24 My chest aches when I lie down. I have not been near an egg. I have not. I checked the scan myself.
[color=#C8EE3C]I CHECKED IT MYSELF.[/color]
